stem: Tanya rinses chalk dust from a duster into a bucket. After standing, some chalk settles, but fine particles still make the water cloudy. She can pour off (decant) the upper liquid or filter it through a fine cloth. The cloth has small pores. She also has a coarse tea strainer.

statements.text: Fine chalk particles that keep the water cloudy need filtration through a fine cloth, not decantation alone.
A coarse tea strainer will remove chalk particles smaller than its holes.
The fine cloth holds back solid particles and lets the liquid pass through its small pores.

teacher.key_rationale: Decantation alone leaves fine suspended particles. Filtration through a fine cloth separates them because small pores hold solids back. A coarse strainer cannot remove particles smaller than its holes.
